feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads well overall, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with strong evidence of increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack), which boosts credibility.  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, skills, and experience; positioning is consistent and targeted.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially in the freelance role and earlier positions (e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); consider consistent date formatting (“Sept.”/“Oct.”), and replace slash styling in “Digital Media Manager / Producer” if not intentional. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: emphasize digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector or advocacy organizations.
- Tighten the list of channels; “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” is slightly repetitive and can be streamlined.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Expertise spans web and CMS modernization, content operations, email, social, analytics, and multimedia, with a strong record of building scalable workflows and governance systems. Experienced in advocacy and stakeholder communications, translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content and digital experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “advocacy messaging” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Cross-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Group related items and remove vagueness: “Web platform governance & CMS administration,” “Editorial systems & workflow design,” “Analytics, reporting & performance insights.”
- Align wording with recent experience and target roles by foregrounding strategy, governance, and platform modernization over production.
- Suggested version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially strategy, analytics, multimedia, and workflow themes.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the few contributions that best extend—not repeat—your NACo leadership experience.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and communications operations for enterprise public-facing channels.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations into one outcome-focused line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more specific and results-led: “Designed and launched modular Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, reusable content sections, and member toolkits.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites, users, publishers, turnaround time, engagement lift.
- Keep the AI search bullet, but sharpen it: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the NACo Director role; keep only what is new or more advanced here.
- Detailed project examples may duplicate the Recent Projects section; avoid repeating the same wording.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with an outcome-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate channel oversight bullets and lead with the biggest win: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, production volume, reporting cadence, engagement growth, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed as scaling/building institutional capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge than a distinct achievement-focused role. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine newsletters and audience into one sharper bullet: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Strengthen process language with clearer impact: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”  
  If possible, add metrics: send volume, open rates, video cadence/views, publishing turnaround, or number of teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” may duplicate governance/operations language in the Director role.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the prior NACo role; distinguish this one as scaling/owning the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and planning systems” to better match the seniority shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, add one signal of scale, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially repeat Core Competencies and the header.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, with most relevant/recent items first.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint, Power Pages and WordPress
- Airtable-based content and operational systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- If space allows, replace “technical execution” with “platform modernization & implementation” for a more senior tone.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority platform if this section needs to feel more selective.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” As a topline skills item, it should emphasize decision-making value and outcomes, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools after the capability terms: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten wording and group related items: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and leadership reporting”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO and performance analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT
- Avoid repeating every tool here if they are already listed in Technical + IT; use this section to signal strategic strength instead

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent operational leadership rather than generic task terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event operations • Studio buildout and management • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event delivery”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the in-house studio achievement.
- Change “Livestreaming” to “Livestream and hybrid event operations” for stronger scope and professionalism.
- If space allows, align with tools already listed elsewhere by keeping this focused on capability, not software.

- This section repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” from Core Competencies; use sharper wording here or remove one version.
- “Studio operations” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are supported mainly by older roles, so avoid over-expanding them unless tied to the 2022–2024 studio leadership.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this line to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeat the same tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by relevance/recency: Drupal first, then WordPress, then SharePoint/Power Pages/GitHub Pages.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it reads lighter than the rest of the stack.
- If accurate, add version/scope for strongest platform: e.g., Drupal 9/10 or “enterprise Drupal.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus CMS modernization.
- Avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here unless you remove it from Topline Skills and make this the primary platform section.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent work and modernize older terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless tooling: Cloudflare Workers • Dev workflow: GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping “jQuery” or moving it to the end as “legacy support with jQuery” so it doesn’t date the profile.
- Use consistent category labels instead of a flat list; this improves scanability and signals practical application rather than basic familiarity.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/context elsewhere on the CV (e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”), since this line itself can’t show impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want a more engineering-oriented signal.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add light qualifiers to show depth: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project operations)”
- Consider trimming to the strongest, most relevant tools used recently; keep older or lighter-use platforms off this line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same concept in multiple sections without added specificity.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; include them only if they materially support your systems/operations positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and underplays a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. Make it more specific to platform depth and audience/engagement use cases.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, Member Engagement & Journeys
- Replace with: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope cues: enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, segmentation, automation/journey building, member communications
- Optional stronger version: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp • Email automation • Segmentation • Newsletter operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” is vague and overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; use “Member Engagement” or “Email Marketing.”
- Avoid repeating newsletter/email impact here if it’s already covered well in NACo experience bullets; keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs without repeating website/video points already covered above.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Make leadership more specific: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored/supervised a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving cross-channel workflows for web, email, social, and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “Website refresh” overlaps with the later full redesign; avoid sounding like the same project.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, keep this focused on foundational project coordination and the first-podcast achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and “firsts”: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Tighten the digital-content line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types/volume of projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language used in later NACo roles unless you can specify a distinct format or outcome.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia leadership here; that is already stronger and more credible in the 2015–2024 roles.
